issues.description: Normalization only handles ClassName nodes; ignores escaped IDs, attribute selectors, and tag/pseudo selectors with equivalent escape ambiguity
issues.detail: normalizeNodeEscaping only branches on parser.isClassName(node). The same escape-equivalence issue applies to ID selectors (#u-m\+ vs #u-m\00002b), attribute selectors, and pseudo-classes/elements with escaped identifiers. The PR title and changelog claim a general fix for 'escaped selectors' but the implementation narrows coverage to class names only, leaving symmetric false negatives. Either broaden the helper to all node types whose value-getter/setter normalizes escaping, or scope the changelog and tests to class selectors only.

issues.description: Early-return on missing raws.value may skip normalization for nodes that still need it
issues.detail: The guard `if (!node.raws?.value) return;` assumes that if raws.value is absent, node.value is already in canonical form. This relies on internal behavior of postcss-selector-parser: when raws.value is unset, the stored value is what was parsed. If a node's value was set programmatically by an earlier rule transform (without populating raws), normalization may be skipped even when needed. Verify against the parser source or remove the optimization until benchmarked — correctness should not depend on an undocumented invariant.

issues.description: Test coverage missing for combined/compound selectors and nested cases
issues.detail: Reject tests cover only simple `.u-m\xx {}` forms. Add cases for compound selectors (`.a.u-m\+`, `.u-m\+:hover`), descendant combinators (`.a .u-m\+`), selector lists within one rule (`.u-m\+, .u-m\00002b {}`), and nested @media to prove the walker reaches all relevant nodes. Without these, the fix's generality is unverified.

issues.description: Self-assignment idiom is fragile and obscures intent
issues.detail: `node.value = node.value` is a clever exploit of getter/setter side effects but relies on postcss-selector-parser preserving this exact behavior across versions. A future refactor of the parser that decouples raws bookkeeping from the setter would silently break normalization with no test failure outside this exact escape case. Consider either pinning a minimum parser version with a comment, adding a unit test specifically guarding the round-trip, or factoring out a tiny `renormalizeValue(node)` helper that's easier to swap if upstream changes.

issues.description: Walker now does two function calls per node where one composite would do
issues.detail: The walk callback was a direct reference to normalizeSelectorNodeWhitespaceAndComments. It now constructs an arrow that calls two helpers per child. For large stylesheets with many selectors this doubles per-node call overhead. Not a blocker, but consider inlining or letting the existing walker just do one pass that handles both concerns, or short-circuit normalizeNodeEscaping early for non-ClassName nodes (already done) so the cost is mostly one isClassName check.

issues.description: Changeset labeled 'minor' but the change is a bug fix
issues.detail: The changeset entry uses `"stylelint": minor` while the description begins with 'Fixed:'. Stylelint's convention (per other recent changesets) is `patch` for bug fixes. Verify against repo policy; if patch is correct, the release will be incorrectly bumped to a minor version.

issues.description: @ts-expect-error comment risks silently breaking if upstream types add raws
issues.detail: If postcss-selector-parser later exposes `raws` in its type definitions, the `@ts-expect-error` directive will start failing the TypeScript check. This is the intended TS behavior, but worth a follow-up note or use of `@ts-ignore` only if the project policy permits. Alternatively, declare a narrow local type extension to access raws without suppressing the diagnostic.

dissents.topic: Scope of normalization: class-only vs all node types

positions.position: The reported issue (#3972) is about class selectors. Ship the minimal fix that closes the bug; expand later when concrete reports come in. Broadening now risks regressions in less-tested paths.

Escape equivalence is a property of all CSS identifiers, not just class names. Solving one node type leaves a footgun where the same rule still false-negatives on IDs and attribute selectors. Either generalize or document the limitation in the rule's docs and changelog.
The idiom is concise and directly leverages library behavior; renaming/wrapping it would add ceremony without changing semantics. The eslint-disable plus comment is sufficient signaling.

The pattern depends on a non-obvious side effect of a third-party setter. Future maintainers (and future parser versions) may not preserve it. Wrap behind a named helper and pin a tested parser version range.
Most class selectors won't have raws.value populated; skipping them avoids unnecessary work in the hot path of a linter that runs on large codebases.

The optimization conflates 'no raws.value' with 'already canonical', which is an undocumented invariant. Until proven by a parser-level test, prefer always normalizing and benchmark before optimizing.

review.summary: The fix is small, targeted, and uses a legitimate (if slightly clever) postcss-selector-parser behavior to normalize CSS escape sequences in class selectors. The reject tests demonstrate the bug closure. Two notable concerns: (1) the fix is scoped to ClassName nodes only, leaving the same false-negative pattern intact for ID, attribute, and pseudo selectors despite a general-sounding changelog; and (2) the changeset is marked `minor` for what reads as a bug fix, which may produce an incorrect version bump. No clear P0 blockers, but expanding coverage (or narrowing the changelog), verifying the changeset bump level, and adding compound/list test cases would meaningfully strengthen the PR before merge.
